extracted.intended_audience: researchers, policy-makers, and research funding organisations interested in grant peer review and gender bias
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and description of the multi-stage peer-review evaluation process used by the EUROCORES funding scheme (outline proposals, external reviews of final proposals, and final panel recommendations), and the factors/criteria that affect selection and scoring. Useful for understanding evaluation criteria, procedural requirements, and covariates considered in funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-stage EUROCORES evaluation process
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation consisted of three consecutive stages: (1) Expert Panels evaluated Outline Proposals (OPs) and selected projects to be invited to submit Final Proposals (FPs); (2) FPs were sent to at least three anonymous external reviewers for written reports and scores; (3) Expert Panels met again to make final recommendations for funding based on the application, referees' comments, applicants' replies and discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 1: face-to-face panel meetings over 1–2 days; panels ~12 members; decisions made through consensus building. Stage 2: written reports from ≥3 referees, 4 weeks typically allowed; Stage 3: panels use reviewers' reports as a main basis for decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel evaluation (Outline Proposal) — binary selection
rubrics_metrics.description: At the first stage, Expert Panels made binary decisions on outline proposals (selected vs. not selected) to invite Final Proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel decisions are made in face-to-face meetings via consensus; panel members act as spokespeople for proposals (each member spokesperson for three proposals ≈ at least nine individual projects). Factors such as consortium size, number of participating countries, cognitive proximity, and prior EUROCORES success influenced selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: External reviewer evaluation (Final Proposals) — scored assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Proposals were assessed by external reviewers who completed a standardized evaluation form and assigned scores (5-point Likert scale) and written comments for each section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each FP was sent to at least three anonymous referees; typically one reviewer evaluated one project on each occasion; reviewers had ~4 weeks to provide assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardised reviewer evaluation form sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers completed a standardized evaluation form comprising 8–10 sections, each focusing on different criteria such as scientific quality, project feasibility, team interdisciplinarity, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two questions (scientific quality of the proposal and qualifications of the PIs) remained unchanged across the period and were used as a proxy for scientific merit in statistical analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring scale for reviewer assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: For each section of the reviewer form, a score was assigned on a 5-point Likert scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study uses the average of scores assigned to scientific quality and qualifications of PIs as a proxy for scientific merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum written justification for reviewer answers
rubrics_metrics.description: For each question/section on the reviewer form, reviewers were required to provide comments in a dedicated space (at least 100 words for each question).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These written reports were used both qualitatively (sentiment and evaluative terms) and quantitatively (to check consistency with scores).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: External reviewers were anonymous referees when assessing Final Proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymity of reviewers is implemented in the external review stage, though the authors note anonymizing applicants is only a partial solution because evaluators need applicant identity for bibliometrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panels should consider reviewers' reports as main basis
rubrics_metrics.description: EUROCORES guidelines state the reviewers' reports should be considered as constituting the main basis for expert panel evaluations at the final recommendation stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel decisions at the third stage were strongly associated with reviewers' scores, in line with this guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: at least three external reviewers per FP
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Final Proposal was sent to at least three different external reviewers to obtain written reports and scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This multiplicity supports aggregation of independent assessments; the second-stage dependent variable is observable only for proposals that passed the first stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer time allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically, the referee had 4 weeks to provide a written assessment of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This timeframe indicates the expected turnaround for external reviews and affects workload and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus decision-making by panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert panel decisions were made through consensus building, involving interaction among peers within the scientific group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consensus-based selection implies deliberation can mediate or amplify signals from reviewers and panel members' proximities/relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific quality of the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: A core criterion assessed by reviewers (one of the unchanged questions) concerning the scientific merit and quality of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the study as part of the proxy for scientific merit (averaged with qualifications of PIs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of the Principal Investigators (PIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: A dedicated criterion evaluating the qualifications and track records of PIs leading individual projects within a consortium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This question remained consistent across years and was averaged with scientific quality scores to proxy scientific merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A reviewer criterion focused on whether the proposed research project is feasible given its plan, resources, and timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the substantive sections on the standardized reviewer form (part of the 8–10 sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Team interdisciplinarity / research diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the degree to which the project team combines different disciplines or research backgrounds (research diversity/interdisciplinarity, measured in analysis by Blau index).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interdisciplinary composition was one of the formal criteria on review forms and a covariate in models; diversity sometimes correlated with selection outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium scientific productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: A bibliometric indicator: total number of publications of the consortium normalized by consortium size (in logs), used to assess productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher scientific productivity was associated with higher reviewer scores in the study; constructed from Web of Science data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation of highly cited scientists
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the consortium includes one or more highly cited scientists (a bibliometric marker of elite expertise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a consortium-level covariate; associated with evaluation outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive proximity between applicants and evaluators
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of overlapping Web of Science subject categories between consortium members and evaluators—used to measure how close the applicants' expertise is to panel/external reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cognitive proximity positively influenced panel decisions in some models, but closeness to evaluators could be penalized by external reviewers (confirming prior literature).

rubrics_metrics.name: Network proximity (prior co-authorship ties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator of whether the consortium and evaluators have at least one common co-author prior to the grant application (network proximity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Network proximity had a positive role in selection (consistent with 'old boy' networks) and was included as a covariate in models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium seniority (average age)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average age of consortium members (in logs) used as a proxy for seniority and experience within the team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seniority was included among covariates that might affect panel/reviewer decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium size
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of participating PIs / size of the consortium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consortium size was an important determinant of success in panel selection according to the study's results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of participating countries
rubrics_metrics.description: The count of different countries represented within the consortium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A larger number of participating countries was positively associated with success in panel selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the consortium includes at least one member affiliated with a university in the Top 100 Shanghai Ranking (used as a binary marker of institutional reputation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a covariate; institutional reputation can affect evaluator judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships with the private sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the consortium includes at least one member with a private sector affiliation (indicator of industry linkage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among factors that might influence evaluation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget requested
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of funding requested by the consortium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a covariate in statistical models to account for scale/resource requests affecting assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous EUROCORES experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the consortium includes at least one member having a prior EUROCORES-granted project before application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior success with EUROCORES had a positive influence on panel decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluator characteristics (gender, productivity, age, institutional reputation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes of panel members and external reviewers—gender, scientific productivity, age, and institutional reputation—considered as covariates influencing evaluation outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study examined these characteristics to assess their role in scores and selection; e.g., share of female evaluators ~20%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel workload and panel size
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel-level procedural factors including the number of proposals per spokesperson and overall panel workload/size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel size and workload influenced outcomes (panel workload had an effect; other panel characteristics were not significant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer text-based evaluation (sentiment and evaluative terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative dimensions of reviewer reports measured via sentiment polarity (VADER) and presence of evaluative lexical terms (bi-grams derived from Word2vec), e.g., 'internationally recognized', 'highly qualified'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study constructed sentiment and evaluative-term indicators to compare with numeric scores and found inconsistencies: sentiment/evaluative terms were largely unrelated to the gender composition effect seen in scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum text length for reviewer reports included in text analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer reports with fewer than 15 words were removed from textual analyses (pre-processing rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textual analyses also removed stop words and infrequent words (<5 occurrences) and formed bi-grams for evaluative-term identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized quantitative methods for dealing with selection bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample selection bias from the sequential evaluation process was addressed using Heckman’s two-step estimation procedure in modelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the methodological expectation for proper statistical handling of sequential selection when analysing multi-stage peer review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to justify scores in writing (consistency expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers were expected to justify numeric scores with textual comments; the implicit criterion is consistency between qualitative language and quantitative scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study found a discrepancy: reviewers' written language did not reflect the negative gender-based differences evident in scores, implying an expectation (and failure) of score–text alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy consideration: informing evaluators ex-post about observed biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that panels and reviewers be informed ex-post about any biases observed in their decisions as a potential corrective measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors argue anonymizing applicants is only partial; increasing evaluator awareness via feedback on bias might change future behaviour.
